graph.name: Suggest the next scene beat
graph.description:
Suggest a plausible next action tied to an unresolved scene hook.

Lesson: Inspect recent-message retention and omissions, then ask Response Plan for one consequence the established cast can cause. A hook is evidence; a proposed next beat is Guidance. Focus Purpose is inactive in Select.

Limitations: There is no deterministic stall classifier or turn-trigger router in this base recipe.

Opening installs an unassigned copy. Bind local model roles and provide the documented evidence before running.

Pre: at most 1 auxiliary calls. Preview before publishing or applying.

Try changing:
Replace Sol's condition with a different established concern, such as returning a borrowed key; check that the plan advances that cause.
Request a quiet pause instead of an immediate offer in the plan; compare pacing without introducing a new threat.

Documentation specimen (does not seed chat or actor memory):

Situation: The players have circled the same locked chest for several turns. Its owner is nearby.

Direction: Let the owner offer a condition for opening it. Move the existing conflict forward; keep acceptance with the player.

Source → selected cause: The two left nodes prepare evidence, not a turn counter. This recipe runs when assigned; it contains no automatic stall detector or trigger router.

Interpretation → delivery: The plan takes at most one local Analysis request. Its NPC initiative is optional writing advice; the Guidance terminal makes the delivery budget separately editable.

Chest and owner (pre-scene)
Purpose: Read eight exchanges plus the selected character so the stalled conversation and the owner's motive share one Context.
Fixture: Character: Sol owns a locked chest and wants his stolen map returned before opening it. Chat: Rowan has inspected its lock twice and asked what is inside. Sol remains beside the chest. No one has accepted a bargain.
Inspect: Confirm both the chest question and Sol's map concern are present. An older motive outside this window must be supplied through supported context, not guessed.

Retain the existing hook (pre-focus)
Purpose: Select supplied Context deterministically using the recent-message protection, literal pins and token target; remove oldest nonmandatory messages first.
Inspect: Compare selected messages with the original. Keep recent 3 protects the recent loop; this node does not classify a scene as stalled. Purpose and the completion cap do not affect Select. Retention follows keepRecent, literal pins and oldest-message removal; semantic relevance belongs in a model-backed step.

A condition, then an opening (pre-plan)
Purpose: Produce one forward beat from an unresolved hook rather than a list of unrelated complications.
Inspect: Expect a condition connected to the map and an unanswered offer. A proposed condition is not a settled transaction or newly discovered chest content.

Output tokens includes visible text and any reasoning tokens counted by the provider. A truncated result is discarded; inspect the error, then manually raise the cap and rerun. No automatic retry occurs.

One causal beat (pre-guidance)
Purpose: Deliver the proposed hook continuation with enough room for its reason and the player response boundary.
Inspect: Check that the Host result contains one actionable direction. The normal host reply remains responsible for the final dialogue and pacing.

pre-focus.title: Context Focus
pre-focus.purpose: Retain the locked chest, Sol's ownership, the missing map, prior questions and all unaccepted terms. Remove unrelated travel discussion first.

pre-plan.title: Response Plan
pre-plan.instructions: Use the locked-chest scene. Sol wants his stolen map returned and controls his chest. Suggest one short causal next beat: he offers a condition for opening it, or explains what evidence would satisfy him if the offer was already made. Label Existing hook, NPC initiative, Open response. Refer only to supplied facts. Do not introduce an attack, stranger, timer, secret contents or recovered map. The player owns Rowan's acceptance and action. Move one step, then stop with a specific question or offer Rowan can answer. Label any newly proposed bargain as optional; never present it as an already-existing offer or bargain.
